bull.t: Sustained revenue growth and margin expansion
bull.b: Strong organic growth combined with faster earnings expansion indicates broad demand and operating leverage across Stryker’s portfolio. Higher margins can support continued investment in product development, commercial execution, and acquisitions while strengthening earnings power over the next several quarters.

bull.t: Strong cash generation and improving leverage
bull.b: Substantial operating and free cash flow gives Stryker internal funding for innovation, acquisitions, and shareholder returns without relying solely on external financing. Deleveraging further improves financial flexibility, although disciplined capital allocation remains important given the company’s absolute debt.

bull.t: Broad product innovation and commercial momentum
bull.b: A steady cadence of launches and rising utilization of key platforms can deepen surgeon and hospital adoption while expanding Stryker’s addressable markets. Greater use of installed systems may also support recurring procedure-linked consumables and durable customer relationships.

bear.b: The disruption directly reduced sales and created backorders in an important product area, showing that operational interruptions can affect customer access and near-term growth. Although management expects improvement by the end of Q3, recovery timing and permanently lost procedures remain execution risks.

Residual remediation and production-related costs can continue to pressure earnings even as reported sales and margins improve. Ongoing spending also absorbs management attention and resources that could otherwise support innovation, commercial execution, or other strategic priorities.

bear.t: Meaningful debt and uneven cash conversion
bear.b: Although leverage has improved, the sizable debt balance leaves Stryker exposed to higher financing needs if acquisition activity increases or operating conditions weaken. Cash flow below EBITDA also indicates that working-capital or cash-cost effects can periodically reduce financial flexibility.
